analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 5232-5676), and the file change is documentation only. I found no executable code, config, key handling or protocol change in the supplied evidence. The text describes MiMo and GLM tensor-parallel decode, speculative MTP rounds, placement, and GLM media and pipeline bounds. It does not claim any trust-boundary behavior change.

Security-relevant statements I checked against the threat model:
- Tensor-parallel sums are sealed with AES-256-GCM on the keyed JACCL plane. Peer pieces that fail to open fail the request. Pipeline boundaries above the raw limit require an authenticated data plane, with no raw fallback (lines 5469, 5625-5629). This is consistent with TB-002 and TB-007 and weakens nothing.
- GLM TP prefix cache (line 5469): entries are tenant-partitioned via prefixScope and prefixDiskScope. The SSD tier is described as encrypted and reached through a second sealed vote, in the same partition. This matches the T-041 posture (salt-scoped entries, encrypted SSD tier). It adds no new at-rest artifact class, but the new GLM TP SSD tier code lives outside the supplied evidence (prefix-cache.md#glm-tp-prefix-ssd-tier). Whether it uses the same HMAC lookup tags and the same TTL is unverified. I recommend a check against T-041 and SEC-035.
- GLM media (line 5475): digest-checked leader and rank-0 preparation, a bounded 32 MiB command, bit-for-bit result verification, and media requests that skip the prefix cache. These are bounded-input controls and no regression is visible.
- Lines 5309 and 5469 state that the GLM width-invariance switch and the load policy are bound into the load agreement. Both Macs' services must set matching values. This is an availability and consistency matter, not a confidentiality one.
- The text states the unmeasured and unqualified status of MiMo TP and GLM2048 and makes no production claims (lines 5258, 5622-5664). It avoids overclaiming, consistent with T-056.

Because only prose is shown, no concrete regression is supported. Residual question: the corresponding code changes (outside these units) should be reviewed for the GLM TP SSD tier and for the environment-forwarded decode switches.
